Last-Hitting 101

Farming minions is the most reliable way to get gold. Learn how last-hitting works and how to get better at it.

Why CS matters

CS (creep score) is the number of minions and monsters you've killed. You only get gold from a minion if your hit is the one that kills it: the last hit.

Kills feel great, but minions are where most of your gold comes from. A full wave of 6 minions is worth about as much as a third of a kill, and a new wave arrives every 30 seconds, all game long. A player who farms well is often richer than a player with more kills.

How much each minion is worth

MinionGoldNotes
Melee minion20The 3 minions in front. More health.
Caster minion14The 3 ranged minions in the back. Low health.
Cannon minion50 (grows over time)The big one. First appears in wave 3, then every few waves.

Each normal wave is 3 melee and 3 caster minions. The cannon minion comes every 3rd wave until 14:00, every 2nd wave until 25:00, and then in every wave.

Pro tipThe cannon minion is worth more than two melee minions put together. If you can only get one minion in a wave, make it the cannon.

How to last-hit

  1. Don't auto-attack minions all the time. Stand back and let your own minions do the damage.
  2. Watch the health bars. When a minion's health drops to about what one of your basic attacks deals, attack it.
  3. Account for the delay. Every attack has a short wind-up, and ranged attacks take time to fly. Start your attack a little before the minion is low enough.
  4. Use abilities when you'd miss. If two minions are about to die at once, use a spell on one and attack the other.

Practice with our last-hit trainer, or in a Practice Tool game with no enemies, until it feels natural.

Common mistakeAttacking every minion as fast as you can. This pushes your wave toward the enemy tower, where farming is harder and you're easier to gank. Only attack minions you can kill, unless you have a reason to push.

Last-hitting under your tower

When the enemy pushes the wave into your tower, the tower hits the minions hard and steals last hits. Here's the basic rule for most champions:

  • Melee minions take 2 tower shots and then die to one of your attacks. Let the tower hit twice, then attack.
  • Caster minions die to one tower shot. Hit them once before the tower does, then finish them after one tower shot.

Exact numbers change as you buy items, but this pattern works for most champions in the first minutes.

XP: stay close

You get experience from minions that die near you (within about 1500 units, a bit more than a screen width), even if you don't last-hit them. If you're out of range, you get nothing from that minion. Missing a wave because you were wandering in the jungle costs you both gold and levels.

CS goals

A perfect player gets about 10 CS per minute in lane, plus bonus from cannons. You don't need to be perfect. Track your CS at 10 minutes (press Tab to see it):

  • 40-50 CS at 10:00: a fine start for a new player.
  • 60-70 CS: good. You're getting most of your minions.
  • 80+ CS: excellent. This is where strong ranked players are.

Supports are the exception: they shouldn't take minions from their ADC. Junglers count jungle monsters instead.

Key takeaways

  • Only the killing blow (last hit) on a minion gives gold.
  • Melee minions give 20 gold, casters 14, cannons 50 or more: never miss a cannon.
  • Don't attack every minion; wait until it's low enough, accounting for your wind-up.
  • Under tower: melee minions need 2 tower shots, casters need 1 of your hits first.
  • Aim for 60+ CS at 10 minutes as you improve.
